findings.claim: `prewarmModules` must exist as an (optional) property on the `Environment` type, otherwise this is a compile error; the assertion `<Environment>{...}` does not silence excess-property checks.
findings.rationale: TypeScript applies excess-property checking to object literals in type assertions, so adding `prewarmModules: false` fails to compile unless `Environment` declares it. I can't see the type definition in this hunk, so this is a flag-for-verification rather than a confirmed bug; if the field was added in the same change set this is fine, but the property must also be optional or every other built-in environment (jsdom, happy-dom, edge-runtime) and every third-party `Environment` implementation would break.

findings.claim: Hard-coding `prewarmModules: false` for the default `node` environment is a silent behavior/perf change for the most commonly used environment, and it is applied uniformly to both the `setup()` and `setupVM()` code paths.
findings.rationale: `node` is the default environment for virtually all Vitest users, so opting it out of module prewarming changes module load timing/ordering for everyone without an opt-in. It is plausible that prewarming is genuinely useless for plain Node (no DOM globals to patch), but the same flag also governs the `setupVM()` path below, where each test runs in a freshly created `vm` context and prewarming may still be doing useful work. Worth confirming the intent covers both paths, and whether users need an escape hatch to re-enable it. Moderate confidence that this is intentional, low confidence that the VM path was considered.
